children.title: Experimental Distinctions Between Autocatalytic Memory and Template-Directed Heredity

detail.title: Experimental Distinctions Between Autocatalytic Memory and Template-Directed Heredity
detail.summary: Chemical memory based on autocatalytic networks relies on compositional persistence (hysteresis) rather than template-directed information transfer. Thermodynamic frameworks suggest that selection requires distinct separation between functional coding and the metabolic persistence of the network.
detail.reason: Synthesis of thermodynamic foundations with non-equilibrium systems research.

children.title: Compositional Heredity and Error Thresholds in Prebiotic Systems

detail.title: Compositional Heredity and Error Thresholds in Prebiotic Systems
detail.summary: Informational stability in prebiotic systems is contingent upon maintaining a copying fidelity that exceeds a critical error threshold. Below this threshold, mutational meltdown prevents the maintenance of heritable information; however, compositional states in autocatalytic networks can demonstrate a degree of stability that suggests an alternative path for information retention without requiring full templated copying.
detail.reason: Refining the understanding of error thresholds and stability, incorporating the Matsubara et al. analysis of growth-division regimes.
